component.name: a2a
component.title: A2A
component.description: Expose a route as an agent and call remote agents with the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol.
component.label: ai

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelA2AOperation.label: producer
CamelA2AOperation.description: The operation that the producer performs, in place of the operation option: the enum name, such as TASK_GET, or the A2A method name, such as GetTask. For an unknown value, the producer logs a warning and uses the operation option.

CamelA2ARequestOperation.label: consumer
CamelA2ARequestOperation.description: The A2A method of the request that the consumer passes to the route: SendMessage or SendStreamingMessage, as the consumer answers the other methods itself. Also set as an exchange property of the same name.

CamelA2ARequestTaskId.label: consumer
CamelA2ARequestTaskId.description: The id of the task that the consumer created or continues for the request. The reply of the consumer uses the exchange property of the same name, not this header.

CamelA2ARequestContextId.label: consumer
CamelA2ARequestContextId.description: The context id of the request: the contextId of the message, else that of the task that it continues, else a new id. The reply of the consumer uses the exchange property of the same name, not this header.

CamelA2AReplyTaskState.label: consumer
CamelA2AReplyTaskState.description: The state of the task in the reply of the consumer to SendMessage, set by the route, for example TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED. If not set, the task is TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, and an unknown value gives TASK_STATE_UNSPECIFIED. Not used for SendStreamingMessage, whose task ends as TASK_STATE_COMPLETED.

CamelA2AReplyType.label: consumer
CamelA2AReplyType.description: The kind of reply of the consumer to SendMessage, set by the route: task, the default, for a task that holds the reply message, or message for the reply message alone. The consumer does not keep a task that it created for a request answered with a message.

CamelA2ATaskId.label: producer
CamelA2ATaskId.description: The id of the task for the producer operations TASK_GET, TASK_CANCEL, TASK_SUBSCRIBE and the PUSH_CONFIG operations. The producer sets it to the id of the task of the response of MESSAGE_SEND, TASK_GET and TASK_CANCEL. MESSAGE_SEND and MESSAGE_STREAM do not read it: to continue a task, send a Message whose taskId is set.

CamelA2APushConfigId.label: common
CamelA2APushConfigId.description: The id of the push notification config for the producer operations PUSH_CONFIG_GET and PUSH_CONFIG_DELETE, which the producer sets from the response of PUSH_CONFIG_CREATE and PUSH_CONFIG_GET. With protocolBinding HTTP+JSON, these two operations do not read it, and take the task id and the config id from the CamelA2ATaskId header written as taskId:configId.

CamelA2AContextId.label: producer
CamelA2AContextId.description: The context id that the producer sets on the message that it sends with MESSAGE_SEND or MESSAGE_STREAM, unless the body is a SendMessageRequest. The producer sets it to the context id of the task of the response of MESSAGE_SEND, TASK_GET and TASK_CANCEL.

CamelA2AMessageId.label: common
CamelA2AMessageId.description: The id of a message. The consumer sets it to the messageId of the message of the request. The producer sets it to the messageId of a response that is a message, not a task.

CamelA2ATaskState.label: producer
CamelA2ATaskState.description: The state of the task of the response of the producer, for MESSAGE_SEND, TASK_GET and TASK_CANCEL, for example TASK_STATE_COMPLETED or TASK_STATE_WORKING.

CamelA2AMethod.label: producer
CamelA2AMethod.description: The A2A method that the producer called, for example SendMessage or GetTask.

CamelA2AResponseType.label: producer
CamelA2AResponseType.description: The kind of response that the producer received: task, message, taskList, pushConfigList or stream. Not set for PUSH_CONFIG_CREATE, PUSH_CONFIG_GET and PUSH_CONFIG_DELETE, nor with dataFormat RAW. The CamelA2AReplyType header sets the kind of reply of the consumer instead.

CamelA2AReturnImmediately.label: common
CamelA2AReturnImmediately.description: Not used: the consumer looks for it in the HTTP request after it removed every header whose name starts with Camel, so the configuration of the request and the returnImmediately option apply. The producer does not send it.

CamelA2AHistoryLength.label: common
CamelA2AHistoryLength.description: The maximum number of the latest messages of the task history that the remote agent returns, for the producer operations TASK_GET and TASK_SUBSCRIBE.

CamelA2AStreamEmitter.label: consumer
CamelA2AStreamEmitter.description: The emitter of the server-sent event stream of a SendStreamingMessage request, which the route can use to send status updates, artifacts and messages of the task to the client. Only set for SendStreamingMessage.

CamelA2AListContextId.label: common
CamelA2AListContextId.description: Only list the tasks of this context id, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AListPageSize.label: common
CamelA2AListPageSize.description: The maximum number of tasks of the page that the remote agent returns, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AListPageToken.label: common
CamelA2AListPageToken.description: The token of the page of tasks to return, for the producer operation TASK_LIST: the nextPageToken of the previous response, which only dataFormat RAW gives.

CamelA2AListIncludeArtifacts.label: common
CamelA2AListIncludeArtifacts.description: Whether the remote agent includes the artifacts of the tasks, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AListHistoryLength.label: common
CamelA2AListHistoryLength.description: The maximum number of the latest messages of the history of each task that the remote agent returns, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AListStatusTimestampAfter.label: common
CamelA2AListStatusTimestampAfter.description: Only list the tasks whose status changed after this time, an ISO-8601 date-time with an offset, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AListStatus.label: common
CamelA2AListStatus.description: Only list the tasks in these states, a comma-separated list such as TASK_STATE_WORKING,TASK_STATE_COMPLETED, for the producer operation TASK_LIST.

CamelA2AExtensions.label: consumer
CamelA2AExtensions.description: The URIs of the A2A extensions that the client requested in the A2A-Extensions HTTP header and that the agent card of the consumer declares. Also set as an exchange property of the same name.

consumerOut.description: The message of the caller, for SendMessage and SendStreamingMessage (the component answers the task and push config requests itself): the text of its parts, one per line, a data part as JSON and a file part as its URL. With dataFormat POJO the Message, with RAW the Message as JSON

consumerReply.description: The reply of the agent: text, sent as one text part (bytes, a stream or a file as their text), or Message content with the consumer task/context identity. Another body is sent as text: a Task as the text of its last message, a Map or a POJO as its toString(): marshal it first. The reply goes in a Task, completed unless the CamelA2AReplyTaskState header says another state, or as a Message when the CamelA2AReplyType header is message

producerIn.description: The message to send: text, sent as one text part (bytes, a stream or a file as their text), or a Message. Forwarding the original consumer Message instance strips its task/context IDs; route-supplied copies retain theirs. MESSAGE_STREAM also takes a SendMessageRequest. Another body is sent as its toString(), so a Map or a POJO needs marshalling first, and JSON text is sent as text. PUSH_CONFIG_CREATE needs a TaskPushNotificationConfig, and the other operations read headers, not the body

producerOut.description: The reply of the agent as text: the parts of the Message, or of the last message in the history of the Task, one per line. TASK_GET and TASK_CANCEL give the text of the Task, TASK_LIST a List of Task, MESSAGE_STREAM and TASK_SUBSCRIBE an Iterator of the events as they arrive (split it), and the push config operations a TaskPushNotificationConfig, a List of them, or an empty Map for delete. With dataFormat POJO the Task or the Message, with RAW the JSON of the response as text (a stream of the events for MESSAGE_STREAM and TASK_SUBSCRIBE)

agentCardSource.description: Where the agent card comes from: a JSON file on the classpath (classpath:) or in the file system (file:), an http:// or https:// URL that the endpoint downloads the card from when it starts, or a plain name, which is the agent name when no card gives one. A URL that does not end with .json gets the path /.well-known/agent-card.json. The consumer serves the card as its own. The producer calls the URL that the card gives for protocolBinding, or this URL without the well-known path when the card gives none or when apiKey, bearerToken or oauthProfile is set.

agentCard.description: An agent card, usually a reference to an org.apache.camel.component.a2a.model.AgentCard bean in the registry. The fields that it sets replace those of the card from agentCardSource, and the name, description and version options replace its fields in turn.

basePath.description: The path prefix of the HTTP routes of the consumer, also of the path of its agent card, for example /agents/weather. The producer adds it to the URL of the remote agent only when the host option is set. A missing leading slash is added and a trailing slash removed.

dataFormat.description: The form of the message body. PAYLOAD: the text of the message parts, one per line, where a Task of the producer gives the parts of the last message of its history. POJO: the model object, which is the Message of the request on the consumer and the Task or the Message of the response on the producer. RAW: JSON text, which is the Message of the request on the consumer and the response as received on the producer (an InputStream of the events for MESSAGE_STREAM and TASK_SUBSCRIBE), where the producer sets no A2A header but CamelA2AMethod. The reply of the consumer does not depend on it.

description.description: The description of the agent, which replaces the description of the agent card from agentCardSource and agentCard. If the card declares no skills, it is also the description of the default skill of the card.

historyLength.description: Not used: the endpoint only checks when it starts that the value is not negative. The producer takes the history length of TASK_GET and TASK_SUBSCRIBE from the CamelA2AHistoryLength header, and that of TASK_LIST from the CamelA2AListHistoryLength header.

host.description: The host of the remote agent that the producer calls, in place of the URL of the agent card and of agentCardSource, for example for tests. Without an http:// or https:// prefix, https is used. The port and basePath options are added to it. The consumer does not use it.

name.description: The name of the agent, which replaces the name of the agent card from agentCardSource and agentCard. If no card gives a name, a plain name in agentCardSource is used, and the endpoint fails to start without a name.

port.description: The port of the remote agent that the producer calls. Only used with the host option. The consumer does not use it.

protocolBinding.description: The A2A protocol binding. HTTP+JSON is the REST binding, with a path per operation such as /message:send, and JSONRPC posts JSON-RPC 2.0 requests to the base path. The consumer serves only this binding, and the producer calls the URL that the agent card gives for this binding. The aliases rest and jsonrpc are also accepted, in any case.

returnImmediately.description: Whether the consumer answers SendMessage at once with a task in state TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED and runs the route in the background, so that the client polls the task with GetTask. The returnImmediately and blocking fields of the configuration of the request take precedence. With protocolBinding HTTP+JSON, a SendStreamingMessage request for which it is true is rejected. The producer does not use it.

validateAuth.description: Whether the consumer checks the credentials of each request, except the request for the agent card, against the security requirements of its agent card, with the apiKey, bearerToken or oauthProfile option. If true, the card must declare securitySchemes, or every request is rejected. If false, the consumer accepts requests without credentials. The producer does not use it.

version.description: The version of the agent, which replaces the version of the agent card from agentCardSource and agentCard. If no card gives a version, 1.0 is used.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

httpServerComponent.label: consumer,advanced
httpServerComponent.description: The name of the Camel component that serves the HTTP routes of the consumer, which must implement RestConsumerFactory, for example platform-http, undertow or jetty. If not set, the consumer uses the component of the REST configuration (camel.rest.component), else platform-http, else the only RestConsumerFactory among the components or in the registry.

maxConcurrentTasks.label: consumer,advanced
maxConcurrentTasks.description: The maximum number of SendMessage and SendStreamingMessage requests that the consumer processes at the same time. A request beyond the limit is rejected with a ServerBusyError, which is HTTP status 429 with protocolBinding HTTP+JSON, unless it can wait in the queue of taskQueueSize. Use 0 for no limit.

sseHeartbeatInterval.label: consumer,advanced
sseHeartbeatInterval.description: The interval in milliseconds at which the consumer writes a heartbeat comment line (:) to a server-sent event stream that has no event to send, so that proxies do not close the idle connection. Used for SendStreamingMessage and SubscribeToTask.

sseQueueCapacity.label: consumer,advanced
sseQueueCapacity.description: The number of server-sent events that the consumer buffers per stream for a slow client, at least 2. When the buffer is full, the consumer drops a new event and logs a warning, but for the final events of the stream it drops older events instead.

taskQueueSize.label: consumer,advanced
taskQueueSize.description: The number of SendMessage requests with returnImmediately that can wait in a queue, as tasks in state TASK_STATE_SUBMITTED, while maxConcurrentTasks requests are in progress. Only used when maxConcurrentTasks is greater than 0. Use 0 for no queue, so that these requests are rejected at once.

operation.label: producer
operation.description: The operation that the producer performs. The CamelA2AOperation header replaces it for a message.

connectTimeout.label: producer,advanced
connectTimeout.description: The connect timeout in milliseconds of the HTTP connections of the endpoint: the requests of the producer, the push notifications that the consumer sends, and the download of the agent card from an HTTP URL when the endpoint starts. It is also the timeout of the whole download of the agent card.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

streamingReadTimeout.label: producer,advanced
streamingReadTimeout.description: The time in milliseconds that the producer waits for the next line of a server-sent event stream, for MESSAGE_STREAM and TASK_SUBSCRIBE, before it closes the stream with an error. The heartbeat comments of the remote agent count as lines. Use 0 for no timeout.

asyncTimeout.label: advanced
asyncTimeout.description: The timeout in milliseconds of the route that the consumer runs in the background, for SendMessage with returnImmediately and for SendStreamingMessage: the consumer then cancels it and marks the task as failed. Use 0 for no timeout on the consumer. The producer uses it as the timeout of the response to its MESSAGE_STREAM and TASK_SUBSCRIBE requests, where it must be greater than 0, and a fixed timeout of 60 seconds for the other operations.

completedTaskTtl.label: advanced
completedTaskTtl.description: The time in milliseconds that the in-memory task store of the consumer keeps a task after it reached a final state: completed, failed, canceled or rejected. Not used when the registry holds an A2ATaskStore, which the endpoint then uses as its task store.

followRedirects.label: advanced
followRedirects.description: Whether the producer follows HTTP redirects of the remote agent. Disabled by default, as a redirect to another host would also receive the credentials of the producer. The download of the agent card and the push notifications of the consumer never follow redirects.

maxPayloadSize.label: advanced
maxPayloadSize.description: The maximum size in bytes of a request body that the consumer reads, and of a response body or a single server-sent event that the producer reads. The consumer rejects a larger request, and the producer fails the exchange. The agent card has its own limit of 1 MB.

pushRetryAttempts.label: advanced
pushRetryAttempts.description: The number of times that the consumer retries a push notification after a network error or a webhook response with a status other than 2xx and 4xx. A 4xx status is not retried, and 410 Gone also removes the push notification config. Between 0 and 30, where 0 sends each notification once.

pushRetryBackoffMs.label: advanced
pushRetryBackoffMs.description: The delay in milliseconds before the first retry of a push notification, doubled for each further retry and capped at one hour. At most 3600000, and greater than 0 when pushRetryAttempts is greater than 0.

allowLocalWebhookUrls.label: consumer,security
allowLocalWebhookUrls.description: Whether the consumer accepts push notification webhook URLs whose host resolves to a loopback address, such as localhost or 127.0.0.1, also with http. By default these URLs are rejected, like the URLs to private, link-local and other non-public addresses, which this option does not allow. For local development only.

apiKey.label: security
apiKey.description: The API key, for the security schemes of type apiKey in the agent card. The producer sends it in the header, query parameter or cookie that the scheme names, with the Bearer prefix in the Authorization header. The consumer compares the key of each request with it when validateAuth is true.

apiKeyHeader.label: security
apiKeyHeader.description: The name of the header, query parameter or cookie that holds the API key, for a security scheme of type apiKey in the agent card that gives no name.

bearerToken.label: security
bearerToken.description: The bearer token, for the security schemes of type http in the agent card. The producer sends it in the Authorization header when oauthProfile is not set or gives no token. The consumer compares the bearer token of each request with it, also for the oauth2 and openIdConnect schemes, when validateAuth is true and oauthProfile is not set.

oauthProfile.label: security
oauthProfile.description: The name of a camel-oauth profile, for the security schemes of type oauth2, openIdConnect and http in the agent card. The producer gets an access token with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant, from the client-id, client-secret and token-endpoint properties of the profile under camel.oauth, and sends it as a bearer token. The consumer validates the bearer token of each request with this profile when validateAuth is true. Requires camel-oauth, or for the consumer another OAuthTokenValidationFactory.
